title: A smooth zero-mean SST drift of 0.064 K per decade can close five corrected AMIP feedback gaps in 2001-2022
abstract: We calculated the least spatial SST trend that can remove a published AMIP feedback difference while it leaves ocean-mean warming fixed. We used the saved ice-free 60S-60N mask and corrected trends from SCI 64709ea4 and five model response maps. In 2001-2022, the main corrected new-minus-old feedback gap is -0.48346 W m-2 K-1 of ocean SST. A smooth degree-3 spherical harmonic drift closes the mean gap at a minimum area RMS of 0.03079 K per decade. Closing all five model gaps at once requires 0.06384 K per decade, with a peak of 0.17561. The mean-only solution leaves a model gap as large as 0.25186 W m-2 K-1. Across 20 correction choices, smooth simultaneous thresholds are 0.05302-0.07076 K per decade. Independent-cell and nine-region tests give different thresholds. A minimum-norm proof and an independent dual audit certify all 240 solutions across two periods. These are conditional sensitivity thresholds, not measured errors or probability limits. We add no independent SST observations and omit nonlinear, sea-ice and polar effects. The numerical test uses the earlier saved correction set, not the larger later event set. Code, exact input hashes, figures and aggregate certificates support reproduction.

display.caption: Minimum zero-mean spatial trend for feedback-gap closure, and the smooth simultaneous solution. Results are conditional on fixed corrections and five linear response maps.
